newsitem.title: USA: Stephanopoulos going to teach at Columbia.
newsitem.headline: Stephanopoulos going to teach at Columbia.

text.p: George Stephanopoulos, a senior adviser to U.S. President Bill Clinton, will leave the White House to teach political science at Columbia University in New York, White House officials said Tuesday.
The official announcement of the move was expected to be made on Wednesday by the university.
Stephanopoulos, 35, has long signalled his intention to leave the White House after helping Clinton get elected in 1992 then working for him for four years.
Stephanopoulos, a Greek-American whose boyish good looks and hard-charging style made him something of a celebrity, is to start his new job in January. He is a Columbia graduate.

After helping in Clinton's 1992 campaign, Stephanopoulos became White House communications director and held a brief, stormy tenure as the president's spokesman before turning over those duties to then-press secretary Dee Dee Myers.
Behind the scenes as senior adviser, he had a role as a Clinton confidant and worked closely with members of Congress.
